blocking_findings.finding: The profile states false feature values without placing the corresponding repeatable --disable arguments in the frozen argv. These values are therefore descriptive, not mechanically applied.

The treatment MCP definition has no frozen serialization into the actual Codex invocation. Because user config is ignored, the treatment cannot reproducibly obtain exactly the declared Bateia server and bateia_recommend tool from this profile alone.
The declared CODEX_HOME is not auth-only and the declared existing empty cwd is absent.

minimum_focal_refinement: Freeze complete resolved argv arrays separately for control and treatment, not only a common argv plus declarative arm objects.
Add one --disable <feature> pair after exec for every feature declared false, and verify the resolved feature state before dispatch without a model call.

Serialize the sole treatment mcp_servers.bateia configuration into explicit -c key=value arguments or a separately hashed invocation-only config that remains effective under --ignore-user-config; freeze command, args, cwd, required flag, enabled_tools=["bateia_recommend"] and approval mode. The control resolved argv must contain no mcp_servers entry.
Prepare a fresh CODEX_HOME inventory containing only the authentication material explicitly permitted, record its non-secret inventory provenance, and fail if any other state is present.
Create and verify the declared cwd as an existing empty directory before sealing, then hash or otherwise freeze its empty-state receipt.
Rerun only the execution-profile feasibility recut and M-PROFILE-DRIFT first. If it passes, rerun the full positive, opaque, mutation, repetition and reordering gate before a new seal candidate.

seal_decision.rule: Mutation score 1.0 is necessary but insufficient while the executable capability profile is not reproducible and its filesystem preconditions are false.
